text: Experiment zero three: Short circuit. In this experiment, we will learn the effect of a short circuit.
The components required are: a three-volt battery ePod, a red LED ePod, and three jump wires.
Here is the circuit diagram from the workbook. In addition to the normal battery and LED loop, a third jump wire connects directly across the positive and negative terminals of the LED.
First, we connect the normal circuit. Battery positive to LED positive, and battery negative to LED negative. The red LED glows normally.
Now, connect a third jump wire directly from the positive terminal of the LED to the negative terminal of the LED.
Notice that the LED immediately stops glowing! The third wire creates a direct path with very low resistance between the positive and negative poles, bypassing the LED.
In a short circuit, all the current flows through the direct path without obstruction. This generates a lot of heat and can cause fires in household electrical systems.
Important safety warning: Disconnect the short circuit wire after twenty seconds. Never keep a short circuit connected, or the battery will heat up and leak chemicals.
Now, remove the third jump wire. The short circuit is removed, and the red LED glows normally once again.
